newsitem.title: USA: Kimmins sees return to profitability in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Kimmins sees return to profitability in 1997.

text.p: Kimmins Corp said Thursday that while it was disappointed with its just-released 1996 results, it looks for a "strong recovery in 1997."

Francis M. Williams, chairman and president, said the primary contributors to the 1996 results were operating losses from substantially completed projects and costs associated with the mid-year closing of the company's Niagara Falls, N.Y., office.
But he noted that the company's 1996 performance "will not impair our ability to return to profitable performance in 1997, starting in the first quarter."

For its 1996 year ended December 31, the company posted a net loss of $8.683 million or $1.96 a share, compared to a net income of $1.343 million or $.30 a share, for the previous year. Gross revenues for 1996 were $113.24 million against $111.346 million for the previous year.

Net loss for the fourth quarter of 1996 was $7.078 million or $1.60 a share, compare to a net loss of $106,000 or $0.03 a share on revenue of $27.398 million for the quarter against $30.32 million for the comparable period in 1995.
